newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil sees high risk at Vema Dome well.
newsitem.headline: Statoil sees high risk at Vema Dome well.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil ) said on Thursday its planned deepwater well in the Vema Dome area in the Norwegian Sea was still regarded as a high-risk project despite a recent gas discovery in a neighbouring licence.

Last week the Norwegian Oil Directorate (OD) said British Petroleum Norge had found gas from deepwater exploration drilling in the frontier Nyk High area, which lies next to Vema Dome in the Voering Basin.

The OD said it was too early to give precise figures for the size of the find, but preliminary estimates indicated between 40 to 60 million cubic metres of oil equivalent gas, or almost half the size of the North Sea Frigg field.
Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said its exploration would primarily search for oil.

"The Nyk Ridge find confirms that hydrocarbons are present in the area, but we haven't found any proof yet that oil is or has been in the system. However, the reservoir sands have turned out to be of good quality," said Svein Thorbjoernsen, who is responsible for deepwater drilling at Statoil.

Statoil is due to spud on the Vema Dome prospect in block 6706/11 in mid-September. Diamond Offshore Drilling Inc's Ocean Alliance rig will drill the well in about 1,240 metres of water, roughly 300 km northwest of Broennoeysund off the northern Norwegian coast.
The well will be drilled to a depth of 5,000 metres.

Statoil said three-dimensional seismic had been shot over the area since the acreage was awarded in the 15th licensing round last year. High-resolution surveys also have been carried out at the drilling site.
